A Linux networking guide to CIDR notation and configuration

A quick comment on CIDR to give additional depth to the topic, as most posts don't contain enough information to actually understand what it is and why.

CIDR is basically a condensed notation of a netmask, it allows you to express a netmask such as 255.255.252.0 as /22. All it actually is is the number of active bits from the netmask added up to a total. These notations can be converted back and forth when you understand binary a little.

111111111 = 255

111111111 = 255

111111100 = 252

00000000 = 0

This is because: 

1st 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 equals 255
2nd 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 equals 255
3rd 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 equals 252
4th no bits active equals 0

Each bit in an octet has an associated value as you can see. Each octet has eight bits that can either be on or off, with 1 being on. They are the following values:

128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1

To reverse it, as I mentioned CIDR notation represents the number of active bits in the netmask. So if you turn on 22 bits

111111111.111111111.111111100.00000000

And then add the value at each position within each octet into their own total like above, then put it in dotted decimal notation you can express it back as a netmask.

I've skipped a few details and tricks, but if you don't understand or want to understand more please research
